findings.finding: Direct industrial-communications peer HMS Networks (Q3 report 2026-10-21) posted strong demand, with order intake +22% organic (Europe about +20% organic, data centres and semiconductors supporting, global PMI at its highest since 2022), but it also flagged component-cost inflation broadening from memory to PCBs and passives, tariffs broadened over the summer, gross margin down to 62.7% (64.1), price increases only from 1 January 2027, margin pressure into Q4/2027, and about SEK 70m of customer pre-buying. HMS fell 7.6% on the day and a further 4.2% on 10-22, while EPEN rose 3.7% on 10-21: the market took the orders read-across for Ependion and not the margin one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ependion's order line has driven its last two prints up: +18.1% on 2026-04-28 (record order intake 778 MSEK) and +10.3% on 2026-07-15 (orders +24%, EBIT 76.2 vs 71.0 Pinpoint consensus); a margin disappointment drove -13.7% on 2025-04-29 and -29.0% on 2024-10-22 (computed from Yahoo daily closes on the issuer's own release dates).
findings.why_not_priced: The orders half looks priced: EPEN rose 3.7% (150.2 -> 155.8 SEK) on the day HMS reported strong orders. The margin half is not: HMS lost about 11.5% over two sessions on the component and tariff commentary while EPEN gave back only 1.4% on 10-22, and EPEN's 20-day run-up is -1.9%. If the market had applied the margin read, EPEN would have moved with HMS on 10-21/22 rather than against it. Net it is a small negative, because Ependion's own Q2 already disclosed strained component supply and price adjustments. It is a peer proxy, not company-level, and the bar it touches (EBITA, one analyst) is thin, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: Ependion's own Q2 report independently says the component market 'remains strained, with longer lead times and higher prices' and that inventory was built (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bdc2c672b65b80cbcd6f15806121600d8&lang=en&src=listed); Placera/FactSet's preview put HMS's bar at EBIT 248 / orders 1,028, which HMS beat on both, so the sell-off was about the commentary, not a miss (https://www.placera.se/telegram/hms-networks-hms-networks-vantas-redovisa-248-miljoner-kronor-i-rorelseresultat-factset-20261019).

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar (624.85 MSEK, +15% y/y) looks reachable or modestly beatable. The order backlog was 1,319 MSEK at end-Q2 (+20% y/y) after H1 book-to-bill of 1.15, Welotec has been fully in the base since Q3 2025, and SEK translation has turned from FY2025's 'strong currency headwinds' to a tailwind: USDSEK averaged about 9.84 in Q3 2026 against about 9.44 in Q3 2025 (+4%), and EURSEK about 11.20 against about 11.01 (+2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales alone has not been the swing line; in FY2025 the stock fell 2.0% on 2026-01-26 on a report headlined by currency headwinds, and it rose on order beats rather than on sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The backlog is public and the two revenue estimates (618.7-631) presumably model it. What may not be fully in is the size of the FX swing, which consensus revenue at +15% partly reflects. A slight sales beat would show up as consensus at the high end of the range; it is not there, so the size is near zero.
findings.independence: FX from Yahoo monthly series (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/USDSEK=X?range=2y&interval=1mo and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EURSEK=X?range=2y&interval=1mo); HMS also cited 'favorable currency effects' for Q3 2026 in the same SEK reporting currency (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=ba8531e3e7f6afcb07078dd8b36d20e08&lang=en&src=listed).

lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': the HMS orders (+0.7) and HMS margin (-1.0) read-across findings were merged into one netted finding at -0.3.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' (backlog is public): the revenue-bar finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2.

'Size the move on what is new; history moves p_up, not abs_move': abs_move_pct was raised from 8.0 to 8.5 on the name's real report-day distribution and thin turnover; p_up went from 55 to 52 because the one counterparty read is two-sided and its consensus EPS bar rests on a single analyst.
'The session check must open with bmo/amc and cite a URL': it is written that way, with the issuer's 13:00 CEST timestamp.
